clue.text: Antipodean recognised headless spirit with sign of hesitancy

indicators.note: a headless word loses its first letter, here the silent opening of the past tense of know

parts.note: recognised means knew
zeal is spirit or fervour
and means with, together with
er is the sound made when hesitating

explanation.surface: A ghostly figure without a head, hesitating as it is spotted, from the other side of the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipodean describes someone from Australia or New Zealand, the lands on the opposite side of the globe from Britain.

clue.text: Sleep on family's sheets

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep
kin is family, so family's gives kin's

explanation.surface: Someone dozing on the family bedlinen.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Napkins are squares of cloth or paper, sheets used at the table to wipe hands and mouth.

clue.text: Virtue of West player in bridge losing lead

indicators.note: losing its lead means the first letter goes from the bridge seat

parts.note: North is one of the four players at a bridge table

explanation.surface: Praising the merit of the West player at a bridge table, who has just given up the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge players are named by compass points, so 'West' is already a player, misdirecting from its role as plain W.
explanation.definitionFit: Worth is merit or value, which is the sense of virtue as a good quality.

clue.text: Passing light reflected over grass

indicators.note: reflected means the word for light is turned back to front

parts.note: pale means light in colour
to grass is slang for informing on someone, as is to sing

explanation.surface: Light bouncing back over a lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that is elapsing is passing by, a direct synonym in the present participle.

clue.text: Master collie gently bites

indicators.note: bites means the phrase takes a mouthful of letters from within itself, a run hidden across the words

explanation.surface: A sheepdog nipping its owner softly.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege is a feudal lord or master to whom allegiance is owed.

clue.text: Raised game and beat friend, of course

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the combined letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: RU is rugby union
to tan is to beat or thrash
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Of course someone raised their game, beat a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturally and of course are both interjections meaning as expected, obviously.

clue.text: Exercise tempo slow, gym keeping all content

indicators.note: content here is the inside of each word, so the three words keep only their middles, shedding first and last letters

explanation.surface: Advice for a workout: keep the pace slow in the gym and keep everyone happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like happy but means the contents of each word.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise a right or skill is to use it, which is what employ means.

clue.text: Nick computer record for digital tool

parts.note: to nick and to nail are both slang for to arrest or catch
a file is a stored computer record

explanation.surface: Stealing a computer's file to make a digital tool, as if hacking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digital' suggests computers but means of the fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool for shaping fingernails, and fingers are digits, so the tool is digital in the anatomical sense.

clue.text: Bug is way to intercept spy

indicators.note: intercepting means the way cuts into the middle of the spying word

parts.note: to peer is to spy or look closely
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A wiretap is a way to catch a spy's messages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' looks like a listening device in this spy setting but is the verb meaning annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug someone is to annoy them persistently, which is to pester.

clue.text: Chap occupying a hospital ward gets fixed

indicators.note: occupying means the chap sits inside the other letters

parts.note: per means a, as in once per day
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A man takes a hospital bed and is mended.
explanation.definitionFit: Permanent means fixed in the sense of lasting and unchanging.

clue.text: Calm person that's good in school subject?

parts.note: PE is physical education, a school subject
an ace is an expert, someone very good at something

explanation.surface: Asking whether a calm pupil is the one who shines in a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the whole as an ace at PE: an expert in physical education.
explanation.definitionFit: Peace is calm, a state of quiet tranquillity, as a noun.

clue.text: Like a shot at home and can't stand having consumed second

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: having consumed means the dislike word swallows the time unit

parts.note: to hate something is not to be able to stand it

explanation.surface: Someone at home who loathes waiting, having eaten a second helping.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something like a shot is doing it at once, quickly, with speed.

clue.text: Underground part of passage reportedly allowed

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so a word for a passage gives one that sounds the same

parts.note: a route is a way or passage
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A tunnel, so people say, has been permitted.
explanation.walkthrough: ROUTE is said 'root' in British English.
explanation.definitionFit: A rootlet is a small root, a part of a plant that grows below the soil.

clue.text: Criminal don's cruel rogue

indicators.note: criminal means the letters are treated wrongly, set into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A mafia boss is a heartless crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like the definition but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoundrel is a dishonest villain, a straightforward synonym of rogue.

clue.text: Devotee losing fifty deer exaggerates

indicators.note: losing means the Roman numeral is dropped from the fan word

parts.note: a lover of something is a devotee
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
does are female deer

explanation.surface: A wildlife fan who has lost fifty deer is making too much of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who overdoes something takes it too far, overstating or exaggerating it.

clue.text: Sounded relaxed receiving acceptable answer

indicators.note: receiving means the word for relaxed takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: rested means relaxed
on means acceptable, as in that's not on

explanation.surface: Someone sounded relaxed on getting a satisfactory reply.
explanation.definitionFit: Resonated means echoed or rang out, a verb of sound like sounded.

clue.text: Rank river in Italy, not Belgium

indicators.note: not means the country's letter is left out of the river

parts.note: the Tiber flows through Rome
B is the international vehicle code for Belgium

explanation.surface: A river that is in Italy rather than Belgium smells bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like an adjective for a smelly river but is a level.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a level or row, one rank in a series stacked above one another.

clue.text: In posh car, dodgy banker's opening padded envelope

indicators.note: in means the other letters are placed inside the car

parts.note: Jag is short for a Jaguar, a luxury car
iffy means doubtful or dodgy

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A crooked banker in a luxury car handing over a padded envelope of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: A Jiffy bag is a British brand of padded mailing envelope.
explanation.definitionFit: Jiffy bag is the trademark name widely used for a padded envelope for posting.

clue.text: Dance official vocal

indicators.note: vocal means spoken aloud, so the word for official gives one sounding the same

parts.note: real means official or genuine, as in the real thing

explanation.surface: A dance official who is outspoken.
explanation.walkthrough: A reel is a lively Scottish or Irish folk dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is a brisk folk dance, so it is an example of a dance.

clue.text: Tough lifting gold sculpture

indicators.note: lifting in a down clue means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
a bust is a sculpture of head and shoulders

explanation.surface: Raising a gold statue is hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: Robust means strong and sturdy, hard to break, so tough.

clue.text: Jumpers and loafers covering yard

indicators.note: covering means the idlers wrap round the measure

parts.note: skivers are shirkers or idlers, British slang

explanation.surface: Sweaters and slip-on shoes spread over a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumpers and loafers' looks like clothing: a jumper is a British sweater and loafers are shoes; here they are parachutists and shirkers.
explanation.definitionFit: Skydivers jump from aircraft, so they are jumpers in the literal sense.

clue.text: Attacks blocked by foremost of titanium headwear

indicators.note: blocked by means the first letter gets into the attack word and stops it up

parts.note: sets on means attacks

indicators.note: foremost of means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Assaults deflected by a titanium helmet.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stetson is a wide-brimmed cowboy hat, an example of headwear.

clue.text: Satisfy female monarch disheartened with church

indicators.note: disheartened means the heart, the middle letter, is removed

parts.note: a queen is a female monarch

explanation.surface: Pleasing a queen who has lost heart and turned to the church.
explanation.definitionFit: To quench a thirst is to satisfy it.

clue.text: Live event happening involving United and Rovers

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: involving means the letter is wrapped inside the next pair of words

parts.note: a do is a party or event
in means happening, fashionable
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names

explanation.surface: A live match featuring Manchester United and a Rovers side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United and Rovers' look like football clubs, but 'Rovers' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedouin are nomadic Arab desert people, who rove from place to place.

clue.text: Yielding when lacking with regards to protection

indicators.note: when lacking means the following letters are taken out of the yielding word

parts.note: deference is yielding to another's wishes
re means with regard to, concerning

explanation.surface: Giving way when there is no safeguard.
explanation.definitionFit: Defence is protection against attack, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Amusing daughter with sound of drum

parts.note: a drum roll is the sound made by rapid drumbeats

explanation.surface: A funny daughter banging on a drum.
explanation.definitionFit: Droll means wryly funny, amusing in a dry way.

clue.text: Figure on upcoming group of players

indicators.note: upcoming in a down clue means the letters come upwards, read bottom to top

parts.note: ten is a figure, a number
taken as written

explanation.surface: A number about to be announced for a team.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a group of nine musicians playing together.

clue.text: Hard stone terrine regularly used

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the dish is taken

explanation.surface: A rock-solid pâté that has been eaten often.
explanation.definitionFit: Stern means severe or harsh, the hard sense in a hard line.

clue.text: Moment right to return doctor's instruments

indicators.note: to return means the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: Bones is a nickname for a doctor, so doctor's gives Bones's, shortened to the name

explanation.surface: A doctor coming back just in time to collect his equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: Bones is slang for a doctor, from sawbones; the possessive 's is part of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Trombones are brass instruments with a sliding tube.

clue.text: Sloshed night rum explains

indicators.note: rum is old slang for odd or strange, so the letters are put into a strange new order

explanation.surface: A drunken evening on rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink after 'Sloshed', but is the adjective meaning odd.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed light on something is to clarify or make it clear, an idiom for explaining.
